evidence.claim: On the eve of invasion, Putin publicly argued that a Ukrainian nuclear weapons program would be a real danger and an answerable threat, using it to justify heightened security claims.
evidence.title: Путин заявил, что угроза Украины создать собственное ядерное оружие не пустая бравада
evidence.excerpt: On the eve of invasion, Putin publicly argued that a Ukrainian nuclear weapons program would be a real danger and an answerable threat, using it to justify heightened security claims.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Russian state wire reproduces Putin's televised remarks with direct quotations.
contrary_evidence: The claim about a Ukrainian nuclear program was speculative and not established.
It was used as a justification for escalation rather than risk reduction.

evidence.claim: Putin ordered Russia's deterrence forces onto a special alert status, explicitly linking the move to NATO rhetoric and sanctions during the Ukraine invasion.
evidence.title: Putin orders putting deterrence forces on special alert in wake of NATO's aggressive statements against Russia
evidence.excerpt: Putin ordered Russia's deterrence forces onto a special alert status, explicitly linking the move to NATO rhetoric and sanctions during the Ukraine invasion.
evidence.source_locator: lead paragraph and quoted instruction to Shoigu and Gerasimov
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous report with the president's quoted instruction.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct personal order from Putin to the defense leadership
contrary_evidence: Russia portrayed the move as defensive deterrence.
Independent observers treated it as dangerous nuclear brinkmanship.

evidence.claim: Russia temporarily suspended New START inspections, saying the U.S. inspection plan and travel restrictions made the regime look like a provocation and denied parity.
evidence.title: Russia suspends inspections stipulated in New START arms control treaty
evidence.excerpt: Russia temporarily suspended New START inspections, saying the U.S. inspection plan and travel restrictions made the regime look like a provocation and denied parity.
evidence.source_locator: lead paragraphs quoting the Foreign Ministry and Ryabkov
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous state-wire report on an official arms-control suspension decision.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State decision under Putin's presidency; not a private personal remark but attributable to his government
contrary_evidence: Moscow said it remained committed to the treaty's provisions.
Washington said the suspension was irresponsible and destabilizing.

evidence.claim: Putin said Russia would supply Belarus with Iskander-M missiles capable of carrying nuclear warheads and could also upgrade Belarusian aircraft for that role.
evidence.title: Putin promises Belarus nuclear-capable missiles to counter aggressive West
evidence.excerpt: Putin said Russia would supply Belarus with Iskander-M missiles capable of carrying nuclear warheads and could also upgrade Belarusian aircraft for that role.
evidence.source_locator: report body and Putin-Lukashenko meeting summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report on a direct bilateral meeting and a specific capability transfer announcement.
contrary_evidence: Putin and Lukashenko framed the move as symmetrical deterrence, not proliferation.
The practical effect was to deepen nuclear exposure in Belarus.

evidence.claim: The IAEA said explosions hit the Zaporizhzhia plant area and reiterated that a nuclear safety and security zone was urgently needed because the site was in a volatile combat environment.
evidence.title: Update 128 - IAEA Director General Statement on Situation in Ukraine
evidence.excerpt: The IAEA said explosions hit the Zaporizhzhia plant area and reiterated that a nuclear safety and security zone was urgently needed because the site was in a volatile combat environment.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct IAEA incident report describing damage and escalation at the plant.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect attribution through Russian control of the territory and wartime conduct
contrary_evidence: The IAEA did not assign full blame in the text excerpt.
The broader implication remained that Russian wartime control made the site unsafe.

evidence.claim: At the annexation ceremony, Putin invoked Hiroshima and Nagasaki as a precedent and used that argument to justify the annexation speech's broader confrontation framing.
evidence.title: Путин заявил, что США единственные в мире дважды применили ядерное оружие
evidence.excerpt: At the annexation ceremony, Putin invoked Hiroshima and Nagasaki as a precedent and used that argument to justify the annexation speech's broader confrontation framing.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct state-wire report on a live presidential speech with specific nuclear rhetoric.
contrary_evidence: The comparison was rhetorical, not an operational instruction.
It normalized nuclear precedent language in a crisis context.

evidence.claim: The Kremlin said attacks on the annexed Ukrainian regions would be treated as attacks on Russia, while Reuters noted Putin had just threatened nuclear use to defend territorial integrity.
evidence.title: Kremlin says any attack on annexed territory will be an attack on Russia
evidence.excerpt: The Kremlin said attacks on the annexed Ukrainian regions would be treated as attacks on Russia, while Reuters noted Putin had just threatened nuclear use to defend territorial integrity.
evidence.source_locator: lines around the Peskov quote and annexation summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report relayed by Euronews, with a specific attributable Kremlin quote and immediate nuclear implication.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct state attribution tied to Putin's annexation move and prior nuclear threat
contrary_evidence: Russia claimed this was a legal consequence of annexation.
International actors treated it as coercive nuclear shielding of conventional war.

evidence.claim: The NPT review conference ended without a final document and many delegates condemned the Russian Federation's dangerous nuclear rhetoric and the risks around Zaporizhzhia.
evidence.title: Non-Proliferation Treaty Review Conference Ends without Adopting Substantive Outcome Document Due to Opposition by One Member State
evidence.excerpt: The NPT review conference ended without a final document and many delegates condemned the Russian Federation's dangerous nuclear rhetoric and the risks around Zaporizhzhia.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and delegate interventions in the meeting coverage
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official UN meeting coverage summarizing multilateral criticism of Russian nuclear behavior and plant risk.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Russian Federation under Putin's war leadership
contrary_evidence: Russia argued the meeting still had valuable discussions and blamed others for the failure.
The dominant multilateral reading was that Russian conduct was the source of the risk.

unresolved_gaps: Direct evidence on command-and-control discipline, custody, accident-prevention, and other nuclear safety procedures in 2022 is thin.
Direct evidence on expert governance and risk institutions is weak relative to the rhetoric and escalation evidence.
The package needs better household and distribution evidence, not just macro stabilization and state-budget outcomes.
Direct evidence that appointments and institutions translated into durable productivity investment is still thin.
Direct 2022 delivery evidence for health, education, housing, and food security inside Russia remains thin.
Implementation and take-up by region and group are not well documented.
Direct documentary proof of Putin's personal beneficial ownership, asset control, or hidden conflicts remains limited.
The appointment and accountability map is still too thin for a fully rounded honesty judgment.
Direct 2022 implementation metrics for procurement, output, and battlefield effectiveness remain thin.
The package still needs a cleaner separation between frantic adaptation, temporary stabilization, and genuinely effective goal advancement.
